howto.name: Upload a PDF
howto.text: Drop a PDF up to 500 MB.

howto.name: Set an owner password and permissions
howto.text: Choose which operations are allowed for users without the owner password: print, copy text, modify, annotate. If you leave the owner password blank, a random one is used, so nobody can later use it to change the permissions.

howto.name: Download the protected PDF
howto.text: Anyone without the owner password is limited to the allowed operations. The PDF itself still opens without a password (use Protect PDF if you want a user password too).

faq.q: What's the difference between owner password and user password?
faq.a: User password = required to OPEN. Owner password = required to override permissions (print, edit). This tool sets only the owner password + permission flags, so the file still opens without a password. Protect PDF adds an open password, but its owner password is generated at random and never shown.
It's enforced by readers as a courtesy — Adobe Acrobat respects it strictly, some open-source readers ignore it. For real security, encrypt with a user password.
Only if allow_copy is true. If false, the reader disables text selection. Note: screenshots still work (no PDF protection can prevent that).
